title: Romans Bible Quiz - Chapter 6
description: Ten questions on Romans 6: baptism into Christ's death, being dead to sin and alive to God, and the wages of sin against the free gift of God.

questions.text: What answer does the chapter give to the question, "Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?"
questions.explanation: The answer is, "May it never be!" because we who died to sin cannot live in it any longer.

answers.text: "Yes, so that grace may be seen."
"Only until the law is fulfilled."
"That is for each one to decide."
"May it never be!"

questions.text: Into what were all those baptized into Christ Jesus baptized, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: It asks whether they do not know that all who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death.

answers.text: Into the law of Moses
Into his death
Into the name of the apostles
Into the hope of Israel

questions.text: Why were we buried with him through baptism into death?
questions.explanation: It says this was so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we also might walk in newness of life.

answers.text: So that the law might be established
So that sin might abound no more in the world
So that we also might walk in newness of life
So that we might be counted among the circumcised

questions.text: What does the chapter say was crucified with him?
questions.explanation: It says our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away with.

answers.text: Our old man
The law of sin
The flesh of the nations
Our hope of glory

questions.text: What does the chapter say about Christ, who has been raised from the dead?
questions.explanation: It says that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more, and death no longer has dominion over him.

answers.text: He will die once more for the sin of the world
He dies no more, and death no longer has dominion over him
He reigns over the law that was given to Moses
He is a foreshadowing of the one to come

questions.text: How does the chapter tell us to consider ourselves?
questions.explanation: It says to consider yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord.

answers.text: Alive to sin, but dead to the law
Servants of the law, but free from grace
Dead to the flesh, but alive to the nations
Dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus

questions.text: What does the chapter say we should present our members to God as?
questions.explanation: It says not to present your members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but to present yourselves to God and your members as instruments of righteousness.

answers.text: Instruments of righteousness
Instruments of unrighteousness
A living sacrifice on the altar
Servants of the letter of the law

questions.text: Whose servants are you, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: It says that when you present yourselves as servants and obey someone, you are the servants of whomever you obey, whether of sin to death or of obedience to righteousness.

answers.text: The servants of the law you were given
The servants of those who taught you
The servants of whomever you obey
The servants of your own flesh

questions.text: What do those have who are made free from sin and have become servants of God?
questions.explanation: It says they have their fruit of sanctification and the result of eternal life.

answers.text: Freedom from righteousness and from the law
Fruit of sanctification and the result of eternal life
The reward that is owed to them for their works
A share in the law that was given to Moses

questions.text: What does the chapter say the wages of sin are, over against the free gift of God?
questions.explanation: It says the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

answers.text: Shame, while the gift of God is honor
Bondage, while the gift of God is the law
Wrath, while the gift of God is peace with men
Death, while the free gift of God is eternal life
